profile.reading:
Csquare IAD1-B sits at 45845 Nokes Boulevard, Sterling, Virginia 20166, one of three buildings (IAD1-A, IAD1-B, IAD1-C) on Csquare's IAD1 campus in Loudoun County's Northern Virginia data center corridor. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists IAD1-B individually at 37,878 square feet sellable, 49.6 percent leased as of March 31, 2026; Csquare's public spec sheet gives only a combined campus total across all three IAD1 buildings, 141,621 square feet of raised floor, 143.2 megawatts of utility power, 19.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 37.5 megawatts of generator capacity, with chilled-water cooling and SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, ISO 27001, and ENERGY STAR certifications applicable campus-wide rather than broken out per building. All three IAD1 buildings are leased rather than Csquare-owned, per the SEC filing. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date for IAD1-B; Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County as a matter of public record. Loudoun County's data center corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing operators within a few miles of the IAD1 campus.

Csquare's Sterling, Virginia IAD1 campus sits within Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, alongside dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and the same filing notes the company's legal predecessor entity, BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, was formed in May 2018 as a Brookfield Infrastructure Fund III vehicle, well before the 2024 Cyxtera and Evoque combination that produced the assets tracked in this dataset.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement

reading.body:
Csquare IAD1-B is one building on a three-building campus in Sterling, Virginia with a combined 143.2 megawatts of utility power and 141,621 square feet of raised floor. The campus sits in Loudoun County's data center corridor, the world's largest concentration of data center capacity, served by Dominion Energy. Csquare's S-1 filing shows IAD1-B individually at 37,878 square feet and 49.6 percent leased as of March 31, 2026, but the operator publishes power and cooling capacity only for the full IAD1 campus, not per building.

At an assumed 40 kilowatts per rack for AI training loads, the campus's 143.2 megawatts of utility power represents roughly 3,580 racks. The facility holds SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II certifications, PCI-DSS compliance, NIST 800-53 PE High physical security standard, ISO 27001 information security certification, and ENERGY STAR qualification. These certifications permit hosting regulated workloads and demonstrate availability and security controls, though the operator does not publish which tenants are present.

In Virginia, 330 facilities are mapped but only 23 publish power capacity. Csquare's IAD1 campus ranks 24th statewide by published megawatts, with Virginia's 23 published facilities totaling 1,375.4 megawatts. The IAD1 campus's power comes leased from three buildings rather than Csquare-owned real estate. Csquare's full portfolio of 64 facilities across 21 markets holds 389 megawatts total, making this Northern Virginia location part of the company's largest regional footprint but not yet its largest single facility.
